examples.knowledge_point: Dividing a Complex Number by an Imaginary Number
examples.problem: If $z_1 = -8-3\textrm{i}$ and $z_2 = 2\textrm{i},$ then what is $z_1$ divided by $z_2?$

feedback.worked_solution:
The denominator is $6+2\text{i}$ and its conjugate is $6-2\text{i}.$ We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $6-2\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{6+2\text{i}} & =\frac{5}{6+2\text{i}}\cdot \frac{6-2\text{i}}{6-2\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{30-10\text{i}}{36-12\text{i}+12\text{i}-4{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{30-10\text{i}}{36-4{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{30-10\text{i}}{36-4(-1)} \\  & =\frac{30-10\text{i}}{36+4} \\  & =\frac{30-10\text{i}}{40}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{30-10\text{i}}{40}=\frac{30}{40}-\frac{10}{40}\text{i}=\frac{3}{4}-\frac{1}{4}\text{i}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
